text:
Colorado State University | Fort Collins, CO

M.S. in Water Resources | August 2025 - December 2026

Pennsylvania State University | State College, PA

B.S. in Environmental Resource Management | August 2017 - May 2021




ROSSyndicate Lab | Watershed Science and Water Quality Technician | May 2026 - Present

Collects and prepares water quality field samples. 



Installs, operates, and maintains in-situ sensors and data loggers. 



Reviews and cleans historic water quality data in R. 

SWCA Environmental Consultants | Environmental Scientist | June 2022 - May 2025

Leads and assists with project management tasks, such as writing proposals, budgeting, client coordination, and managing technical tasks for various projects, including water resources and renewables projects. 



Writes environmental assessment reports which detail the findings of field surveys and convey pertinent environmental regulations to our clients. 



Analyzes and QA/QC field data from site visits to interpret in environmental assessment reports. 



Conducts site assessment surveys to identify sensitive environmental resources on future project sites, specifically aquatic resources, migratory birds, and mammals. 

CMS Environmental Consultants | Environmental Analyst | November 2021 - June 2022

Routinely inspected erosion and sediment control measures at 40-50 commercial, residential, and industrial construction projects in the Denver Metro area. 



Wrote inspection reports following each site visit detailing site findings which were then used to correct potential pollutant discharges off site. 



Routinely communicated with clients and regulators to relay inspection findings and discuss solutions for pollution prevention on client’s sites. 
Reviewed and audited stormwater pollution prevention plans (SWPPPs) for each client’s site to ensure that their plans were compliant with COR400000 and Denver city regulations. 

Penn State Sustainable Ag, Food, and Environmental Science Institute | Intern | June – September 2021 

Analyzed GIS mapping data and conducted site visits, with the County Conservation District, of a local watershed for the Chesapeake Bay Foundation through ArcGIS to identify current and future sites for BMP implementation. 



Responsible for creating, leading, and obtaining partners for two stakeholder education workshops, one for the Homeowner’s Guide to Stormwater Management and another for a stream health citizen science tool, FISH. 
Conducted water and fish samplings around Lancaster watersheds to analyze water quality and stream health following BMP implementation. 

Penn State Ag and Environment Center | Intern | January - May 2021 

Demonstrated analytical skills by conducting a literary review on the effectiveness of stream, wetland, and floodplain best management practices (BMP), compiled summaries, and presented results. 



Responsible for analyzing GIS mapping data of three local watersheds through Google Earth Pro and ArcGIS to identify current and future sites for BMP implementation. 



Individually conducted site assessments to check the viability of future BMP locations from GIS data. 

U.S. Environmental Protection Agency | Office of Compliance Intern | June - August 2019 

Input, tracked, and analyzed trends in excel with data from the ten EPA Region’s National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Compliance Monitoring Strategy (CMS) reports, compiled results, and presented to the Office of Compliance Water Branch. 



Collaborated with two team members to learn wiki markup code to input training documents for EPA’s Stormwater Inspector Training Library webpage for stakeholder use. 
Redesigned the EPA’s Drinking Water Compliance Resource Center SharePoint site for consistency. 

Nuclear Energy Institute (NEI) | Governmental Affairs Intern | June - August 2018 

Attended Congressional committee hearings pertinent to NEI and composed hearing reports. 



Organized the company’s Political Action Committee (PAC) database. 



Collaborated with the Governmental Affairs division to complete routine office tasks. 




Penn State Department of Plant Science | Research Assistant | September 2018 - January 2019 

Scanned 150-200 Phaseolus roots to discover stress tolerance mechanisms. 



Organized and labeled the scanned roots according to phenotype and phosphorous levels. 

Penn State Department of Biology | Assistant Lab Teaching Assistant | August - December 2019 

Assisted 40 students and 2 TAs with lab set up, procedures, and instruction for BIO 220W Lab. 



Attended weekly meetings to discuss upcoming lab content and assignments.

title: Maggie Rouin
text:
Maggie Rouin is a first year graduate student in the Professional Science Masters program at Colorado State University studying Water Resources. She is currently working in the ROSSyndicate Lab as a Watershed Science and Water Quality Technician. Prior to attending CSU, she worked in environmental consulting for four years in water resources and renewable resources. Maggie hopes to work in water quality research following the completion of her masters degree. When she’s not studying or working, Maggie spends most of her time in nature either trail running, snowboarding, or cycling.

title: Projects
text:
Lab 1 - Exploring Streamflow Across the Colorado River Basin
Retrieved 44 years of daily streamflow directly from the USGS NWIS API using dataRetrieval. Joined gauge metadata using relational keys — and verified every join. Normalized by drainage area to enable fair comparisons across the basin. Detected low-flow threshold exceedances using rolling statistics for operational drought monitoring. Aggregated by water year and season the natural temporal units of western hydrology. Visualized basin-wide trends with a standardized anomaly heatmap and a flow-weighted spatial center analysis. Modeled the upstream-downstream relationship at the Compact’s accounting point. Evaluated model assumptions and identified the outlier year the model couldn’t predict
Lab 2 - The Geometry of Place: Spatial Analysis Skills for Environmental Science
Built spatial datasets from three different sources: a CRAN package (tigris), a data package (rnaturalearth), and a downloaded CSV. Transformed coordinate reference systems and selected a projection appropriate for national-scale distance analysis. Manipulated geometry types — understanding when to use st_union vs. st_combine, and why casting to MULTILINESTRING is required before computing distances to borders. Computed four sets of distances using st_distance() and stored them as labeled unit vectors. Visualized spatial patterns with continuous color scales, gghighlight, and ggrepel. Built an interactive web map using leaflet to present distance data to a general audience
Lab 3 - National Dam Inventory (NID): From Counts to Local Clustering
Tessellating surfaces to discretize space. Geometry simplification to expedite expensive intersections. Writing functions to automate repetitive reporting and mapping task. Point-in-polygon counts to aggregate point data
Lab 4 - Palo Iowa Flooding
Using remote sensing data we Identify an area of interest (AOI): identified the temporal range of interest and the relevant images, downloaded the images, analyzed the products.
Lab 5 - Machine Learning in Hydrology
In this lab we explored predictive modeling in hydrology using the tidymodels framework and the CAMELS (Catchment Attributes and Meteorology for Large-sample Studies) dataset. Specified a recipe, dropped it into a workflow, and compared multiple models via workflow_set against cross-validated resamples. Extracted variable importance and interpreted predictor ranks through the geographic-proxy lens. Evaluated with spatial cross-validation and reported the honest gap between random and spatial CV. Tuned hyperparameters with tune_grid() and a named grid, then finalized with last_fit().



Presentation
Streams play an important role in communities, providing a source of drinking water, infrastructure, recreation, and ecosystems for aquatic life. Within Larimer County, Colorado, the Cache La Poudre River primarily serves as a source for drinking water, agriculture, and recreation for approximately 400,000 members within the watershed (CPRW 2026). Stream health within this watershed is affected by everyday impacts, such as the agricultural and urban land uses, and by major disturbance events such as the Cameron Peak Fire in 2020. These land use and disturbance events drive nutrient and sediment loading into the stream which can threaten the health of the stream and its ecosystem. To understand these impacts, stream metabolism can be used to evaluate the physical, biological, and chemical conditions of a stream and therefore is a strong indicator of stream health (Reed et al. 2021).
The Cache la Poudre runs through varying land uses, from the mountainous, rocky areas in the upper reaches to the urban and agricultural uses in the middle and lower reaches. The variability of this stream reach allows for a diverse system to analyze its metabolism. The primary measurements that will be utilized when analyzing stream metabolism in this paper are dissolved oxygen and temperature across four sampling locations. This study aims to answer: How does the metabolism of the Cache la Poudre River seasonally vary from the upper to the lower reaches? To address this, I compare metabolism rates across seasons at four sampling locations, starting below Chambers Reservoir through to the CSU Environmental Learning Center. I also assess longitudinal trends across sites and evaluate potential drivers of observed patterns in stream metabolism.
